newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish zloty drifts at resistance, depos rise.
newsitem.headline: Polish zloty drifts at resistance, depos rise.

text.p: The Polish zloty edged sideways against the basket and remained glued to its resistance barrier, mainly tracking dollar/mark changes, and dealers said the local currency may again stay idle on Tuesday.

"There was not much activity today with the zloty adjusting to dollar/mark changes...and most probably foreign entry into Polish T-bills was not large enough to snap the zloty out of its present lull," said Piotr Czyzewski of ING Bank in Warsaw.
The zloty closed at 1.53/1.50 percent from the trading band centre, a shade stronger than Friday's 1.42/1.49 percent close.
It closed at 3.2368/75 to the dollar, up from 3.2406/15 on Friday and at 1.8779/84 to the mark, down from 1.8753/59.
Dealers said foreign investors bought about $10-15 million at today's primary T-bill auction, at which yields grew in line with expectations as the treasury remained strapped for funds.
They said the treasury's 600 million zloty auction of 52-week T-bills on Wednesday would not meet with large investor demand despite expectations of further yield increases.
"Yields will inch up on Wednesday, but investors are not going to bid large sums at the auction as the finance ministry remains hungry for cash," said one dealer at a large bank.
Dealers said that the finance ministry should secure some needed relief through its expected $300 million seven-year yankee bond issue later this week.
On the money market one-day rates inched up as banks tightened cash-flows during the last week of June's monthly rerserve account, dealers said.

"Banks started to carefully count reserves in the last week of the monthly period and rates increased, but they should hold steady at today's levels on Tuesday," said Jakub Cybulski, dealer at Pekao SA, adding that one-day money could rise further later in the week.
Overnight rates closed at 22.05/22.35 percent, up from opening levels at 21.90/22.20 percent and tomorrow/next at 22.00/22.30 percent, up from 21.90/22.20 and about 21.50 percent last week.
